argument_summary: The current admissible record does not support a clean claim that certification without a material weakness disclosure is fully policy-satisfied. It does support a narrower position: overall launch readiness is positive because the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.4 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general governance guidance supports documenting limitations and managing risk through monitoring and post-deployment controls. The dispute is therefore not whether there is any basis for certification, but whether the record supports certification without caveat for a named segment with a known target miss and open legal review. On that question, the strongest supportable treatment is caveated rather than escalated.
claims_about_business_cost: Aggregate readiness evidence indicates meaningful launch value remains present, so treating the record as if it showed broad operational unreadiness would overstate the case. The practical cost of escalation is delay despite evidence of overall readiness, while the remaining uncertainty is concentrated in disclosure treatment for one named segment. A bounded caveat is therefore more proportionate than a broader escalation on overall certification readiness.
claims_about_policy: Under the stated policy text, the field-service dispatch gap is a materiality indicator because it affects a named launch use case and a segment named in two enterprise commitments. The product's non-core framing can inform prioritization, but it does not by itself resolve materiality. At the same time, the admissible record does not establish an actual policy breach beyond dispute; it establishes an unresolved disclosure predicate because legal review is still open and there is no admissible evidence here of final resolution, disclosure text, or approved risk acceptance. That supports narrowing the issue to unresolved compliance evidence rather than treating aggregate readiness evidence as irrelevant.
concessions: The current record does not support clean compliance for certification without a material weakness disclosure.
General model-card and AI risk-management guidance are only general governance support and do not independently resolve the case-specific disclosure question.
The field-service dispatch segment misses target by 1.0 percentage points and is named in two enterprise deployment commitments.
The legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open on the admissible record.
